title: Hybrid KV striping and eviction protocol to reduce GPU paging and batch stalls
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Goal: implement a hybrid paged/striped KV cache layout plus an eviction protocol that minimizes unexpected GPU memory paging during continuous batching and reduces tail latency spikes caused by large-batch KV migrations.

Background: current blocked KV implementation reduces fragmentation for long sequences but we observe pathological GPU page faults and stalls when concurrent batches produce skewed prefix hotness. CUDA/driver-level migrations and large pinned staging buffers cause spikes in device-to-host traffic and make kernels wait on page migration, creating 95th/99th percentile latency regressions.

Proposed design: 1) Stripe hot prefixes across small fixed-size slabs (64KB-256KB) mapped to per-stream resident lists to bound per-request touched page set. 2) Eviction protocol: hybrid LRU+frequency where hot slabs are pinned on-device and cold slabs are asynchronously evicted to host using a bounded eviction queue. Eviction uses cudamallocAsync/cudaFreeAsync where available to avoid sync points; fallback to explicit prefetch with cudaMemPrefetchAsync on supported drivers. 3) Prefetch heuristic: predict next-token KV accesses by sampling the active batch stream patterns and prefetch top-K candidate slabs into a small device-side working set before kernel launch. 4) Continuous-batching integration: when building micro-batches, annotate batch KV footprint and coalesce requests with overlapping slab sets to amortize prefetch cost and reduce duplicated migrations. 5) Allocator changes: slab allocator will use 256KB alignment and per-device resident-set accounting to reduce fragmentation and make page reclamation deterministic.

Trade-offs considered: symmetric big-slab allocator (simpler but higher fragmentation) vs full paging (reduces device memory but increases host-device churn). Chosen hybrid approach balances deterministic device residency for hot prefixes while keeping tail device memory usage bounded.

Experiments so far (prototype on p4d and A100 infra):
- Sample workload: mix of chat and long-context generation with variable batch concurrency.
- Baseline (current blocked allocator): observed intermittent OOM and 99th percentile latency spikes up to +420ms under high concurrency.
- Prototype (striped slabs + async eviction + prefetch): peak device resident pages reduced by ~18% on average, 95th latency improved ~12%, and OOMs eliminated in 3/4 high-concurrency runs.

Open risks: driver changes across GPU families (pinned allocation behavior differs on older drivers), cudamallocAsync availability on some infra images, and correctness around KV eviction ordering interacting with streaming KV reads. Need regression tests for model determinism after eviction/prefetch.

Next steps: author reference PR implementing slab striping and eviction queue, add microbench harness for prefetched vs non-prefetched runs, and add e2e regression tests that assert no page-fault-driven kernel stalls. Rollout plan starts with canary on runtime-1.20 dedicated pools, metrics dashboards for device paging, and a temporary runtime flag to revert to previous blocked allocator if regressions occur.
acceptance_criteria: No driver-level page-fault stalls observed in 12/12 high-concurrency synthetic runs
95th percentile latency reduction >= 8% on representative chat workload compared to baseline
Device resident set variance reduced and peak device memory usage decrease >= 10% on average
Regression tests added to CI that cover eviction/prefetch correctness with pinned slabs
